subject: inefficiencies in deep hierarchical model + interpreting warning message

messages.author: de6fb7786d893b5c
messages.subject: inefficiencies in deep hierarchical model + interpreting warning message
parts:
Hi Stan Developers,

Thanks for all your hard work on a great tool. I've been tweaking the model below for several months now. It gives reasonable posteriors, but is extraordinarily inefficient, taking ~24 hours to run on close to 9k observations from ~900 individuals. I'm also getting warnings about divergent transitions (37 after the last run @ 2500 iterations w/1250 warmup), despite bumping adapt_delta up to .95. I know I could benefit from additional vectorization, but have a hard time figuring out how to do it, given that I'm dealing with different numbers of observations for each participant.

I've recently added some code that's designed to estimate the relationship between some of the sampled parameters, and am now getting a warning message that I can't quite interpret. I suspect that I can ignore it, given that the message's suspected culprit is a linear transformation, but want to be sure. 

Any help on improving the efficiency or interpreting the error would be much appreciated.

data {
  int<lower=1> n; //number of obs
  int<lower=1> p; //number of participants
  int<lower=1> groups; //number of racial groups
  int<lower=1> conditions; //number of conditions
  int<lower=1> group_conds; //number of race*condition combos
  int c[group_conds]; //group condition indicator
  vector[n] y; // observed vals
  int s[p]; //number of obs per participant
  vector[n] t; //observed time
  vector[p] pre_score; //observed pre_scores
  int race_cond[p]; //participant race_cond[p]
}

parameters {
  real b_intercept[p]; //starting point for student j
  real b_time[p]; //slope for student j
  real b_pre[p]; //pre_score coef for student j
  real<lower=0> sigma_i[p]; //variance for student j
  real intercept_i[group_conds]; //intercept for group i
  real time_i[group_conds]; //slope for group i
  real pre_i[group_conds]; //pre_coef for group i
  real intercept_k[conditions]; //intercept for condition k
  real time_k[conditions]; //slope for condition k
  real pre_k[conditions]; //pre_coef for condition k
  real mu_time_raw; //mean slope
  real mu_int_raw;  //mean starting point
  real mu_pre_raw; //mean pre score coef
  real perf_int[group_conds]; //estimated intercept of lm(b_intercept~b_time)
  real perf_slope[group_conds]; //estimated slope of lm(b_intercept~b_time)
  real<lower=0> perf_err[group_conds]; //error for lm(b_intercept~b_time)

  real<lower=0> mu_time_scaler;
  real<lower=0> mu_int_scaler;
  real<lower=0> mu_pre_scaler;
  real<lower=0> time_k_scaler;
  real<lower=0> intercept_k_scaler;
  real<lower=0> pre_k_scaler;
  real<lower=0> time_i_scaler;
  real<lower=0> intercept_i_scaler;
  real<lower=0> pre_i_scaler;
  real<lower=0> b_intercept_scaler;
  real<lower=0> b_time_scaler;
  real<lower=0> b_pre_scaler;
  real<lower=0> perf_int_scaler;
  real<lower=0> perf_slope_scaler;
}

transformed parameters {
  real p_time[p];
  real p_intercept[p];
  real p_pre[p];
  real est_int[p];
  real g_time[group_conds];
  real g_intercept[group_conds];
  real g_pre[group_conds];
  real perf_int_g[group_conds];
  real perf_slope_g[group_conds];
  real c_time[conditions];
  real c_intercept[conditions];
  real c_pre[conditions];
  real mu_time;
  real mu_int;
  real mu_pre;

  mu_time <- mu_time_raw * mu_time_scaler;
  mu_int <- mu_int_raw * mu_int_scaler;
  mu_pre <- mu_pre_raw * mu_pre_scaler;

  for (i in 1:conditions) {
    c_time[i] <- mu_time + time_k[i] * time_k_scaler;
    c_intercept[i] <- mu_int + intercept_k[i] * intercept_k_scaler;
    c_pre[i] <- mu_pre + pre_k[i] * pre_k_scaler;
  }

  for (i in 1:group_conds) {
    g_time[i] <- c_time[c[i]] + time_i[i] * time_i_scaler;
    g_intercept[i] <- c_intercept[c[i]] + intercept_i[i] * intercept_i_scaler;
    g_pre[i] <- c_pre[c[i]] + pre_i[i] * pre_i_scaler;
    perf_int_g[i] <- perf_int[i] * perf_int_scaler;
    perf_slope_g[i] <- perf_slope[i] * perf_slope_scaler;
  }

  for (i in 1:p) {
    p_time[i] <- g_time[race_cond[i]] + b_time[i]*b_time_scaler;
    p_intercept[i] <- g_intercept[race_cond[i]] + b_intercept[i]*b_intercept_scaler;
    p_pre[i] <- g_pre[race_cond[i]] + b_pre[i]*b_pre_scaler;
    est_int[i] <- (g_intercept[race_cond[i]] + b_intercept[i]*b_intercept_scaler) + ((g_pre[race_cond[i]] + b_pre[i]*b_pre_scaler)*pre_score[i]);
  }

}

model {
  vector[n] nu;
  vector[n] sig;
  vector[p] nu_2;
  vector[p] sig_2;
  int pos;
  int target;
  pos <- 1;
  target <- pos;
  mu_time_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  mu_time_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  mu_int_raw ~ normal(0,1);
  mu_int_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  mu_pre_raw ~ normal(0,1); 
  mu_pre_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  b_intercept_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  b_time_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  b_pre_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  time_i_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  intercept_i_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  pre_i_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  time_k_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  intercept_k_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  pre_k_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  perf_int_scaler ~ normal(0,1);
  perf_slope_scaler ~ normal(0,1);

  for (i in 1:conditions){
    time_k[i] ~ normal(0,1); //implies ~ normal(mu_time, time_k_scaler)
    intercept_k[i] ~ normal(0,1); //implies ~ normal(mu_intercept, intercept_k_scaler)
    pre_k[i] ~ normal(0,1); //implies ~ normal(mu_pre, pre_k_scaler)
  }

  for (i in 1:group_conds){
    time_i[i] ~ normal(0,1); //implies ~ normal(time_k, time_i_scaler)
    intercept_i[i] ~ normal(0,1); //implies ~ normal(intercept_k, intercept_i_scaler)
    pre_i[i] ~ normal(0,1); //implies ~ normal(pre_k, pre_i_scaler)
    perf_int[i] ~ normal(0,1);
    perf_slope[i] ~ normal(0,1);
    perf_err[i] ~ normal(0,1);
  }

  for (i in 1:p){
    target <- target+s[i];
    sigma_i[i] ~ normal(0,1);
    b_intercept[i] ~ normal(0, 1); // implies ~ normal(intercept_i, b_intercept_scaler)
    b_time[i] ~ normal(0, 1); // implies ~ normal(time_i, b_time_scaler)
    b_pre[i] ~ normal(0, 1); // implies ~ normal(pre_i, b_pre_scaler)
    nu_2[i] <- perf_int_g[race_cond[i]] + perf_slope_g[race_cond[i]]*p_time[i] + perf_err[race_cond[i]];
    sig_2[i] <- perf_err[race_cond[i]];
    while (pos < target){
      nu[pos] <- p_intercept[i] + p_time[i]*t[pos] + p_pre[i]*pre_score[i];
      sig[pos] <- sigma_i[i];
      pos <- pos+1;
    }
  }
  est_int ~ normal(nu_2, sig_2);
  y ~ normal(nu, sig);
}

The warning message is as follows:

Warning (non-fatal):
Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    est_int ~ normal(...)

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] inefficiencies in deep hierarchical model + interpreting warning message
parts: You can vectorize almost all of that code.

should just be

time_k ~ normal(0, 1);

If you declare the variables as vectors, this

can be just

p_time <- g_time[race_cond] + b_time * b_time_scaler;

> vector[n] nu;

> ...
> int pos;
> ...
> pos <- 1;

> ...

> for (i in 1:p){
> target <- target+s[i];
> sigma_i[i] ~ normal(0,1);
> b_intercept[i] ~ normal(0, 1); // implies ~ normal(intercept_i, b_intercept_scaler)
> b_time[i] ~ normal(0, 1); // implies ~ normal(time_i, b_time_scaler)
> b_pre[i] ~ normal(0, 1); // implies ~ normal(pre_i, b_pre_scaler)
> nu_2[i] <- perf_int_g[race_cond[i]] + perf_slope_g[race_cond[i]]*p_time[i] + perf_err[race_cond[i]];
> sig_2[i] <- perf_err[race_cond[i]];
> while (pos < target){
> nu[pos] <- p_intercept[i] + p_time[i]*t[pos] + p_pre[i]*pre_score[i];
> sig[pos] <- sigma_i[i];
> pos <- pos+1;
> }
> }

First, I'd sugget putting the initialization before the for loop.
Define variables as late as possible (that is, as close to where
they're used as possible). It's easier to keep the code straight that
way.

Then, you can pull this and all the other ones out of
the loop:

target <- target + s;
sigma ~ normal(0, 1);

and so on.

Does nu and sig get properly defined here for all values?
And why reassign sigma_i to sig?

The trick is to gather everything up that you can and do
everything at once. You can do things like:

nu[pos:pos + s[i]] <- ...
...
pos <- pos + s[i];

and so on.

- Bob
